description: AAC's internals decomposed. AAC (Advanced Audio Coding, MPEG-2 Part 7 / MPEG-4 Part 3) was MP3's successor, designed in 1997 with the benefit of MP3 experience. Pure MDCT (no polyphase), more flexible windowing, TNS, improved psychoacoustics, better Huffman tables. Typically ~30% better compression than MP3 at equivalent quality. Default codec for iTunes, YouTube, satellite radio.

sub_mechanisms.name: aac_profile_lc
sub_mechanisms.definition: Low Complexity profile: AAC core algorithm without prediction tools. The most widely-deployed AAC profile.
sub_mechanisms.why: Removes the optional long-term predictor (LTP) for simpler decoders. Reduces compute ~15% with minor compression cost. Universal for streaming + portable devices.

sub_mechanisms.name: aac_profile_main
sub_mechanisms.definition: Main profile: AAC-LC + Long-Term Prediction (LTP) for additional inter-frame redundancy reduction.
sub_mechanisms.why: LTP catches periodic signals (sustained notes) that single-frame MDCT misses. Marginal compression gain at higher complexity. Rarely used in practice — most encoders just use LC.

sub_mechanisms.name: aac_window_2048_256
sub_mechanisms.definition: AAC uses 2048-input/1024-coefficient long blocks and 256-input/128-coefficient short blocks (8 packed into one 'short-block frame').
sub_mechanisms.why: Twice MP3's window size (1024 vs 576 coefficients) → finer frequency resolution → better masking-based bit allocation. The 8-short-block grouping keeps frame structure consistent at any block configuration.

sub_mechanisms.name: aac_window_switching
sub_mechanisms.definition: Four window types: ONLY_LONG, LONG_START (long→short transition), EIGHT_SHORT, LONG_STOP (short→long transition). Encoder picks per frame based on transient detection.
sub_mechanisms.why: Start/stop windows preserve TDAC across block-size changes (where naive switching would break perfect reconstruction). Per-frame switching matches the transform window to the signal's characteristics.

sub_mechanisms.name: aac_tns_inverse_filter
sub_mechanisms.definition: Temporal Noise Shaping: applies an inverse linear-prediction filter across MDCT coefficients (within one block), shifting quantisation noise toward times where it's masked.
sub_mechanisms.why: MDCT spreads quantisation noise uniformly across the block's time extent. TNS reshapes this noise distribution to follow the signal's temporal envelope — putting noise where signal is loud (and noise is masked) instead of in quiet portions. Particularly effective on speech-like signals in music.

sub_mechanisms.name: aac_scale_factor_bands
sub_mechanisms.definition: Spectrum divided into ~49 scale factor bands (for long block, 14 for short block) aligned with critical bands. Per-band scale factors + Huffman-coded coefficients.
sub_mechanisms.why: Critical-band-aligned partitioning matches perceptual structure better than MP3's uniform partitioning. Fewer bands than MP3 (~21 effective in MP3's hybrid structure) at higher per-band resolution.

sub_mechanisms.name: aac_huffman_codebooks
sub_mechanisms.definition: 11 Huffman codebooks for quantised coefficients (vs MP3's 32). Each codebook handles different coefficient ranges.
sub_mechanisms.why: Fewer codebooks needed because AAC's quantiser gives more consistent statistics across bands. Encoder picks the optimal codebook per scale factor band.

sub_mechanisms.name: aac_intensity_stereo
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-band intensity stereo: above a per-band threshold (often 6 kHz), encoder switches to intensity stereo mode for that band.
sub_mechanisms.why: Same insight as MP3's intensity stereo but applied per scale factor band rather than uniformly. Finer granularity matches the per-band perception model.

sub_mechanisms.name: aac_mid_side_stereo
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-band M/S stereo. Encoder signals per-band whether to code as L/R or M/S.
sub_mechanisms.why: Different bands have different L/R correlation. Per-band M/S exploits where it helps without forcing it where it doesn't. ~5-10% better than always-M/S or never-M/S.

sub_mechanisms.name: aac_noise_substitution_pns
sub_mechanisms.definition: Perceptual Noise Substitution: encoder marks a band as 'noisy' and sends only its energy. Decoder substitutes pseudorandom noise scaled to that energy.
sub_mechanisms.why: Noise-like content has no perceptual structure to preserve. Sending energy + 'use noise' is much cheaper than coding the coefficients. Saves significant bits on noise-dominated bands without audible loss.

sub_mechanisms.name: aac_main_data_no_bit_reservoir
sub_mechanisms.definition: Unlike MP3, AAC frames don't use a bit reservoir; each frame's data is self-contained.
sub_mechanisms.why: Simpler bitstream structure. Tighter rate control per frame but loses MP3's averaging benefit. AAC's better psychoacoustic model + intra-frame tools compensate; AAC at constant bitrate matches or beats MP3 with reservoir.

sub_mechanisms.name: aac_dependent_coupling
sub_mechanisms.definition: Multi-channel coding: dependent channels can be coded as a 'dependently coupled' band, sharing scale factors and coefficients with the primary channel.
sub_mechanisms.why: 5.1+ surround systems have correlated channels (LFE rarely active, surrounds quiet during dialog). Dependent coupling avoids redundant coding of correlated bands. Particularly effective on Dolby Pro Logic-style content.

derivation_rules.name: pure_mdct_simpler_than_hybrid
if: a codec uses pure MDCT instead of polyphase + MDCT
then: bitstream and decoder are simpler at same compression
derivation_rules.why: MP3's hybrid had compatibility reasons; AAC's clean redesign chose pure MDCT for simplicity. Same energy compaction, lower implementation complexity. Direct lineage from MP3 experience.

derivation_rules.name: tns_reshapes_noise_to_match_envelope
if: a signal has temporal envelope variation within a block
then: TNS-shaped quantisation noise is less audible than uniform noise
derivation_rules.why: Quantisation noise that follows the signal's envelope is masked by the signal itself. Flat noise distribution is unmasked during quiet portions of the block, causing audible artifacts. TNS shapes the noise — same total energy, distributed where the signal hides it.

derivation_rules.name: noise_substitution_for_perceptually_noisy_content
if: a band's content is perceptually noise-like
then: sending energy + 'use noise' beats coding the coefficients
derivation_rules.why: Noise content has no structure to preserve. The decoder's synthesised noise is perceptually indistinguishable from the original at fraction of the bit cost. Common on cymbal hits, breath sounds, applause.

derivation_rules.name: per_band_stereo_mode_selection
if: different bands have different L/R correlation
then: per-band M/S vs L/R selection beats uniform stereo coding
derivation_rules.why: Low frequencies often have high L/R correlation (centred mix); high frequencies have less. Per-band selection captures this. Fixed M/S would waste bits on uncorrelated high bands; fixed L/R would miss savings on correlated low bands.

derivation_rules.name: aac_improves_over_mp3_via_compounding
if: a successor codec applies multiple incremental refinements
then: the combined gain is ~30% bitrate reduction at same quality
derivation_rules.why: Pure MDCT + finer block sizes + TNS + better windowing + better Huffman + better psychoacoustic model + noise substitution + per-band stereo. No single feature dominates; the accumulated improvements compound. Same template as H.265 over H.264.
